newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian policeman dies on mountain sortie.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian policeman dies on mountain sortie.

text.p: Egyptian police found on Tuesday the body of a police officer who went missing in the mountains of southern Egypt during a sortie in pursuit of Islamist militants, security sources said.
The officer, Lieutenant Tamer Salah Abdelhamid, 23, had fallen from a ridge and broken his neck, they said.
In a gunbattle during the same sortie on Sunday, at least one suspected militant was killed and three seriously wounded, assistant interior minister Abdelwahhab Abazeid told reporters.
The posse of policemen had to abandon pursuit because nine policemen and four of their civilian helpers had sunstroke.
They called in a helicopter on Monday to search for Lieutenant Abdelhamid but the helicopter could not find him. A foot patrol found his body on Tuesday morning, the sources said.
Police believe they were chasing Islamist militants who killed at least five people in two attacks in the nearby Nile valley on Friday evening.
The sortie was into mountains east of the Nile near the town of Sahel Selim, about 330 miles (205 miles) south of Cairo.
Police believe the gunmen belong to the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), the largest militant group fighting to overthrow the government and set up a strict Islamic state.
More than 1,000 people have been killed since the conflict broke out in early 1992.
